parsed.why: No criminalisation and trans-status anti-discrimination plus hate-crime law on paper, but enforcement is weak: unsanctioned attacks on an LGBT centre, police assault with no sanction, custodial search finding, and a markedly hostile public opinion record.

Currently permissive: self-ID, protected facility access, hate-crime aggravation, conversion ban, marriage equality, high public support. Rollback bills are first-reading only with broad opposition — a real but unresolved trajectory, not yet a traveler-facing restriction.

Decriminalised since 1971, gender-identity discrimination criminal since 2005, working prosecutions, high visibility, no documented traveler-facing exposure. Rising reported hate-crime counts and restrictive minor-care recommendations are resident-side and slightly temper the otherwise strongest protection record.

Same-sex conduct criminalised to eight years with supplementary lashes, marriage criminalised, no protections, hostile official posture, intense social homophobia; but enforcement documented only once in 2015 and resorts report welcoming tourists — episodic, not organised, targeting.

Criminalisation actively enforced — convictions in 2022 and December 2024 with real custodial sentences — plus no discrimination law, chilled civil society, government refusal to decriminalise, pervasive stigma and no documented tourist carve-out; thin record leaves structural signals to extrapolate.
